newsitem.title: INDIA: India Congress opposes foreign firms in insurance.
newsitem.headline: India Congress opposes foreign firms in insurance.

text.p: India's Congress Party said on Friday that it opposed allowing multinational companies to operate in the domestic insurance sector.
Spokesman Vithal Gadgil told reporters the party also opposed allowing foreign firms to take equity stakes in Indian media companies.
Gadgil, speaking after a meeting of the executive committee of the Congress Parliamentary Party, said the group was also against allowing foreign airlines in domestic services.

"The Congress Party has taken positions on some key issues, that we oppose the proposal to allow foreign airlines in domestic services, to allow multinationals in the insurance sector and foreign equity in media," Gadgil said.
Congress, which pioneered India's sweeping economic reforms from 1991, gives make-or-break support to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's seven-month old minority government.
Deve Gowda's 13-party United Front alliance is discussing, but is sharply divided over, the three issues Gadgil said the Congress would oppose.
He said Friday's meeting expressed concern at rising prices, slowdown in economic growth and the fall in exports.
Asked if the criticism of the government's economic policies meant the Congress would oppose next month's annual budget in parliament, Gadgil said: "Do not jump to conclusions."
